contribution: Methods for empirical industrial organization: estimating demand, market power and firm productivity from market data, the foundation of modern structural analysis of competition and mergers
rationale: Recent prizes went to growth, institutions and labor, which leaves empirical IO as a long-overdue field. The BLP demand estimation methods and the Olley–Pakes productivity estimator are used everywhere in academia and antitrust work. Pakes and Berry show up on citation-based forecast lists year after year. Bresnahan's work on market power and entry is the natural third. This is a guess under heavy uncertainty, and I don't know the actual 2026 announcement.
